Rivian opens its first fast-charging hub in Europe

Published 2026-10-07 08:15 UTC

Rivian has opened its first fast-charging site outside North America, a 24-stall hub near Amsterdam that is open to any electric vehicle with a CCS2 connector. The company plans to start European deliveries of its R2 SUV next year.

The site is part of the Rivian Adventure Network, which has more than 100 locations in the US and Canada. Rivian says it chose the Netherlands because of the country's high rate of EV adoption and dense charging demand along motorways.

Charging costs EUR 0.49 per kWh, with lower rates for Rivian owners. The company did not say how many more European sites it plans to open before the R2 arrives.

The hub near Amsterdam has 24 chargers that can deliver up to 350 kilowatts each, and Rivian says it will be open to other electric vehicle brands using the standard European connector. Drivers of non-Rivian vehicles will pay a slightly higher price per kilowatt-hour unless they sign up for a monthly membership.

Rivian plans to open five more hubs in Europe next year as it prepares to sell its smaller R2 SUV in the region. The company says the hubs are located near major highways and include lounges, restrooms and coffee shops, a design meant to make longer charging stops more comfortable.

European charging networks have grown quickly, but drivers still complain about broken chargers, inconsistent pricing and complicated payment systems. Rivian says its hubs will support plug-and-charge, which automatically identifies the vehicle and bills the driver's account without needing an app or card.

Analysts said building chargers before vehicles arrive is a bet that Rivian can establish a premium brand in Europe, where competition from established automakers and Chinese manufacturers is intense. The company has said it will build cars for Europe in a new factory planned for 2027, though it has not finalized the location.
